note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Sands (1972); original in English; the genus has no soldier caste and only alates and workers are described; measurement tables, figure numbers, synonymy and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with all the preceding species in alphabetical order, it is distinguished by the wider meso- and metanotal constriction of the alate and the shorter mixed segment of the worker, and the mandibular proportions of both castes also differ. The two other species of the genus, A. nanus and A. polyscolus, are smaller, and their alates have flatter compound eyes; the workers of both have spinose structures on the enteric valve.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, pilosity yellow, setae sparse. Postclypeus rather strongly raised, Pcl/W 0.31–0.34, Pcl/Ri 2.47–2.67. Mandibular apical teeth short, composite ratio 0.59–0.64, Ra/Ri 0.78–0.82; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible is separated from the molar plate in surface view by a distinct notch, composite ratio 12.20–13.49; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth equal, composite ratio 15.12–18.60. Fore tibia hardly inflated, Ti/Tw 4.51–4.73, the third apical spur about one third the length of the other two, pale and inconspicuous. The midgut-hindgut overlap is short, less than three times the midgut width at the attachment of the Malpighian tubules; the enteric valve base has two very weakly developed opposite lobes and a very small third inner lobe, connected by a short neck to the second hindgut pouch; lateral in the undissected abdomen; the enteric valve cushions are all retracted and of roughly equal development, the surface only scaly; the valve wall bears sparse minute spines between and outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark chestnut brown, not distinctly darker above the fontanelle. Fontanelle reduced, flat, a minute oval spot, slightly paler than the head colour; the median spot circular, flat, slightly larger than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark semicircular, distinctly flat, brown; antennae pale brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotal plates sepia brown, transverse sutures weak or absent; femora brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles sepia brown; sternites pale brown, yellowish brown medially, ventral spiracles brown; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule weakly sinuate, not evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by at most half their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately raised, Pcl/W 0.27–0.31, posterior margin nearly evenly circular, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical teeth short, composite ratio 0.54–0.59, Ra/Ri 0.74–0.82; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible is separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, composite ratio 8.75–9.89; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in one line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than that of the second, composite ratio 19.5–26.5. Head capsule pilosity fairly even, felt-like, interspersed with sparse erect setae, brown. The meso- and metanotal constriction is wider, M/W 0.28–0.31.
